Factorized attention spatiotemporal transformers leverage latent spatial and temporal dependencies in RFID trajectories to predict coverage assignments. They are trained on 10 Hz data and optimized via negative-log-likelihood loss. The model's structure enables efficient processing of high-frequency tracking data, allowing real-time frame-level labeling. Graph neural networks extend this by modeling player interactions as a graph, where nodes represent players and edges represent matchups. This allows for dynamic inference of real-time blocking and coverage patterns. Bayesian multilevel Gamma models introduce hierarchical uncertainty quantification for snap timing, enabling probabilistic inference of quarterback-specific timing skills. These primitives form a coherent framework for situational awareness and predictive analytics in NFL game states.
